version_policy.target: latest stable release, checked each run on python.org
version_policy.verified_against_at_creation: 3.14.6 and 3.13 (latest stable 3.15.2 confirmed on python.org on 2026-11-09; uv did not yet offer a stable 3.15 build)

modules.title: First Contact: Talking to the Computer

chapters.title: Your First Program and Your AI Study Partner
chapters.concept: What a program is, how Python runs code line by line, and the print() function
chapters.why: Every program a computer runs is a list of instructions; learners must see one run before anything else makes sense
chapters.outcome: Run a Python file that prints a short message, read an error message, and use an AI assistant to explain code safely
chapters.ai_skill: Using AI as a tutor that explains, not a machine that does the work; safe prompting habits

chapters.title: Values and Variables: Giving Data a Name
chapters.concept: Values, the types int, float, str and bool, variables and assignment, and arithmetic operators
chapters.why: Programs work with data; naming data lets a program store it, change it and reuse it
chapters.outcome: Store values in well-named variables, calculate with them and predict the result before running
chapters.ai_skill: Asking AI to predict output, then checking the prediction by running the code

chapters.title: Working with Text: Strings and f-strings
chapters.concept: Strings, joining text, f-strings, common string methods and indexing
chapters.why: Most programs show messages, labels and reports to people; text handling is everywhere
chapters.outcome: Build clear, formatted messages from variables using f-strings and string methods
chapters.ai_skill: Writing a precise prompt with an example of the exact output wanted

chapters.title: Talking Back: Input and Type Conversion
chapters.concept: input(), converting text to numbers with int() and float(), and the errors conversion can raise
chapters.why: Useful programs react to the person using them; user input always arrives as text
chapters.outcome: Write a program that asks questions, converts answers and calculates a result
chapters.ai_skill: Giving AI the exact error message and code, and asking for the cause before the fix

chapters.title: Boss Level 1: The Bill Splitter
chapters.concept: Combining output, variables, strings, input and conversion into one small tool
chapters.why: Combining concepts into a working tool is how programming knowledge becomes a skill
chapters.outcome: Build a bill splitter that asks for the total, tip and number of people, then prints each share
chapters.ai_skill: Planning a program with AI before writing it, then reviewing AI suggestions critically

chapters.title: Making Decisions: if, elif and else
chapters.concept: Booleans, comparison and logical operators, if, elif and else, and indentation
chapters.why: Real programs choose what to do based on data, such as approving a payment or showing a warning
chapters.outcome: Write programs that choose between several paths based on input
chapters.ai_skill: Asking AI for edge cases that would break a condition

chapters.title: Repeat Until Done: while Loops
chapters.concept: while loops, loop conditions, counters, break and avoiding infinite loops
chapters.why: Many tasks repeat until a condition changes, such as asking again until the input is valid
chapters.outcome: Write a loop that validates input and stops at the right moment
chapters.ai_skill: Using AI to trace a loop step by step and explain why it never ends

chapters.title: Repeat a Set Number of Times: for Loops and range()
chapters.concept: for loops, range(), looping over strings, and accumulating totals
chapters.why: Processing every item in a group, such as every order or every line, is one of the most common tasks in software
chapters.outcome: Use for loops to process sequences and build totals and tables
chapters.ai_skill: Comparing your loop with an AI-generated loop and judging which is clearer

chapters.title: Debugging with AI: Reading Errors and Tracebacks
chapters.concept: Syntax errors versus runtime errors versus logic errors, reading a traceback, print debugging
chapters.why: Every programmer spends a large share of time finding and fixing bugs; reading errors well saves hours
chapters.outcome: Find and fix bugs of three kinds using tracebacks, print statements and AI help
chapters.ai_skill: A structured debugging prompt: code, exact error, expected result, actual result

chapters.title: Boss Level 2: The Number Guessing Game
chapters.concept: Combining decisions, loops, input validation and the random module
chapters.why: Games are a clear way to combine logic, repetition and user interaction
chapters.outcome: Build a guessing game with hints, attempt limits and input validation
chapters.ai_skill: Asking AI for test scenarios and checking the game against each one

chapters.title: Lists: Keeping Many Values in Order
chapters.concept: Lists, indexing, slicing, adding and removing items, len(), sorting and looping over lists
chapters.why: Real data comes in groups, such as orders, scores or messages
chapters.outcome: Store, change, sort and summarise a list of values
chapters.ai_skill: Asking AI to explain a slice or list method with a worked example you then run

chapters.title: Dictionaries: Looking Things Up by Name
chapters.concept: Dictionaries, keys and values, get(), updating, looping over items, nested data
chapters.why: Most real data has labels, such as a product with a name, price and stock count
chapters.outcome: Model a real record as a dictionary and look up, update and report on it
chapters.ai_skill: Asking AI to design a data structure for a problem, then challenging its choices

chapters.title: Tuples and Sets: Fixed Groups and Unique Items
chapters.concept: Tuples, unpacking, sets, membership tests and set operations
chapters.why: Choosing the right collection makes code simpler and faster, such as removing duplicates with a set
chapters.outcome: Choose between list, tuple, set and dictionary for a given task and justify the choice
chapters.ai_skill: Asking AI to compare options with trade-offs instead of asking for one answer

chapters.title: Comprehensions: Transforming Data in One Line
chapters.concept: List and dictionary comprehensions, filtering, and when a normal loop is clearer
chapters.why: Transforming and filtering data is a daily task; comprehensions make it short and readable when used well
chapters.outcome: Rewrite simple loops as comprehensions and judge when not to
chapters.ai_skill: Asking AI to refactor code, then checking that behaviour stayed the same

chapters.title: Boss Level 3: The Expense Tracker
chapters.concept: Combining lists, dictionaries, loops and decisions into a data tool
chapters.why: Tracking and summarising data is the core of many business tools
chapters.outcome: Build a tracker that records expenses by category and prints totals and the largest category
chapters.ai_skill: Using AI to review your data model and summary logic

chapters.title: Functions: Reusable Blocks of Logic
chapters.concept: Defining functions, parameters, arguments, return values and docstrings
chapters.why: Functions let you write logic once, name it and reuse it; every real codebase is built from them
chapters.outcome: Turn repeated code into well-named functions with clear inputs and outputs
chapters.ai_skill: Asking AI to write a function from a specification, then testing it yourself

chapters.title: Scope and Good Function Design
chapters.concept: Local and global scope, default arguments, keyword arguments, pure functions and single responsibility
chapters.why: Small, predictable functions are easier to test, reuse and hand to an AI for changes
chapters.outcome: Split a long script into small, predictable functions
chapters.ai_skill: Asking AI to identify functions that do too much and suggest a split

chapters.title: Modules and the Standard Library
chapters.concept: import, creating your own module, and useful standard modules such as random, math, datetime and pathlib
chapters.why: Professional programmers reuse tested code instead of writing everything from scratch
chapters.outcome: Organise code into modules and use the standard library to solve common tasks
chapters.ai_skill: Asking AI which standard module fits a task, then confirming in the official documentation

chapters.title: Testing Your Code: assert and pytest
chapters.concept: Why tests exist, assert, writing tests with pytest, edge cases and test-first thinking
chapters.why: Tests prove code works and keep it working when you or an AI change it
chapters.outcome: Write and run tests for your functions, including edge cases
chapters.ai_skill: Asking AI to write tests, then checking the tests actually test the right behaviour

chapters.title: Boss Level 4: The Tested Quiz App
chapters.concept: Combining functions, modules and tests into a structured program
chapters.why: Structured, tested code is what separates a script from software
chapters.outcome: Build a multi-module quiz app with scoring and a passing test suite
chapters.ai_skill: Test-driven work with AI: write tests first, then let AI help with the code

chapters.title: Files and Paths: Saving and Loading Data
chapters.concept: Reading and writing text files with pathlib and with open(), encodings, and CSV files
chapters.why: Data must outlive the program; files are the simplest way to keep it
chapters.outcome: Save program data to a file and load it again, including CSV data
chapters.ai_skill: Asking AI to explain file errors and safe file handling

chapters.title: Handling Errors: try, except and Clear Messages
chapters.concept: Exceptions, try, except, else, finally, raising exceptions and writing helpful error messages
chapters.why: Real programs meet bad input and missing files; good programs fail clearly instead of crashing
chapters.outcome: Make a program handle bad input and missing files with clear messages
chapters.ai_skill: Asking AI to list what could go wrong in your code, then handling each case

chapters.title: JSON and APIs: Talking to Other Programs
chapters.concept: JSON, the json module, how web APIs work, and reading API data with saved sample responses
chapters.why: Modern software exchanges data with other services, almost always as JSON
chapters.outcome: Read JSON data, extract what you need and save results as JSON
chapters.ai_skill: Asking AI to explain an API's JSON response and write code to extract fields

chapters.title: Virtual Environments and Packages
chapters.concept: Virtual environments with venv, installing packages with pip, requirements files and checking package trust
chapters.why: Real projects depend on outside packages and must install the same versions on every machine
chapters.outcome: Create a virtual environment, install a package and record dependencies
chapters.ai_skill: Checking that a package an AI suggests really exists and is trustworthy before installing it

chapters.title: Boss Level 5: The Data Report Generator
chapters.concept: Combining files, exceptions and JSON into a reporting tool
chapters.why: Turning raw data into a clear report is one of the most requested tasks at work
chapters.outcome: Build a tool that reads a JSON or CSV data file, handles bad data and writes a summary report
chapters.ai_skill: Using AI to review error handling and to generate realistic test data

chapters.title: Classes and Objects: Modelling Real Things
chapters.concept: Classes, objects, __init__, attributes, methods and dataclasses
chapters.why: Classes group data with the actions that belong to it, which keeps larger programs organised
chapters.outcome: Model a real-world item as a class and use objects in a program
chapters.ai_skill: Asking AI to design a class, then reviewing whether it fits the problem

chapters.title: Reading and Improving Code with AI
chapters.concept: Reading unfamiliar code, naming, refactoring safely with tests, and reviewing AI changes
chapters.why: Most professional work is changing existing code, often code written by someone else or by AI
chapters.outcome: Understand an unfamiliar program and improve it without changing its behaviour
chapters.ai_skill: A safe refactoring loop: tests first, AI suggestion, review, run tests again

chapters.title: Final Boss: The Personal Task Manager
chapters.concept: Combining classes, files, JSON, exceptions, functions and tests into a complete application
chapters.why: A complete, tested application is proof that you can build software from idea to working tool
chapters.outcome: Build a command-line task manager that saves tasks, handles errors and has passing tests
chapters.ai_skill: Running a full AI-assisted workflow: plan, build, test, review and improve
